title: the WSG artificial illumination slice - the torch wind bands with the lantern and bullseye sighting rules, the magic weapon glows, the campfire radii and the group visibility rules, printed pp. 74-75
audit_label: R485 WSG artificial illumination pin audit
audit_comment: The artificial illumination rules: this section supplements the Players Handbook page 102 statistics with facts relevant to the outdoors. The use of an artificial light source in moonlight or darkness lets characters within the illuminated area see with normal vision as if the natural light was twilight (or perhaps daylight, as with a continual light spell), but the light source's specified radius of illumination takes precedence over the Range of Normal Vision Table figures - a torch holder on a clear night sees only his 40-foot radius, even though in actual twilight under a clear sky he would see 300 yards unaided. Torch: both the radius and the burning time are affected by wind velocity - below 10 mph the PHB figures apply; 11-25 mph the flame struggles and flickers, reliable illumination only out to 30 feet instead of 40 and a burn of 4 turns instead of 6; 26-40 mph the radius is not further reduced but the flame lasts only 2 turns at most, with a 25% chance checked every five rounds of being extinguished and needing reignition; above 40 mph it is impossible to keep a torch burning more than 1 round. Lighting a torch takes 1 round plus 1 per 10 mph of wind, halved with fire building proficiency. In moonlight or darkness a lighted torch can be seen from 200 yards. Lantern: much more reliable in the wilderness - the flame protected, no flicker or wind extinguishing, constant radius; regular lantern light is seen from 100 yards, a bullseye lanthorn beam from 200 yards if the viewer looks directly back toward the source, or 100 yards if his gaze crosses the beam path. Magic weapons: a smaller illuminated area than torch or lantern, but no fuel and no wind effect; the glow is seen from ten times the radius - 100 feet for a magic dagger, 150 for a magic short sword, 200 for a magic long sword. Campfires: small 80-foot radius, medium 120 feet on all sides, large at least 150 feet (perhaps more if especially large). Any artificial light (including magical) in moonlight or darkness limits long-range visibility for everyone within the illuminated area: the lantern holder cannot make out details beyond his 30-foot radius, but someone at the fringe still sees normally into the darkness ahead, and the DM should track who carries light and where the others stand.

banner.title: R485: the WSG ARTIFICIAL ILLUMINATION slice, printed pp. 74-75 - the fourth and final vision-and-visibility round, a pure prose round with NO table, CLOSING the vision chapter: the twilight-as-light frame with the radius-precedence rule and the 40-foot torch vs 300-yard twilight comparison, the four torch wind bands (calm, 11-25, 26-40, above 40) with their radius and burn-time degradation, the 25%-every-five-rounds extinguish risk, the torch-lighting time rule with the fire-building proficiency halving, the lantern and bullseye sighting geometry, the magic weapon glow rule with the dagger/short sword/long sword figures, the three campfire radii, and the group visibility rules with the lantern-holder blind spot and the fringe-sees-normally rule.
banner.provenance: The settle: two-way clean on the first pass - the tesseract full-text read, the pdfy layout read and the tsv coordinate read agree on every number of the page (the wind bands 11-25 and 26-40 mph, the 30/40 feet, the 4/6/2 turns, the 25% and five rounds, the 200/100/200/100 sighting yards, the 100/150/200 magic glows, the 80/120/150 campfire radii, the 30-foot lantern radius); the tesseract /arge for large is an italic-L scan artifact, pdfy reading it cleanly. The section began at the bottom of printed p. 74 (the PHB p. 102 pointer, the twilight frame and the 40-foot torch example, cut mid-word in il-) and its opening prose is pinned with this round. No contested cells, no vision reads needed.
banner.sentinel: Bounds held: the wind bands tile 10-25-40-41 with no gaps, the torch radius and burn time degrade monotonically (40 to 30 feet, 6 to 4 to 2 turns), every magic weapon glow is exactly ten times its radius, and the campfire radii strictly ascend 80 under 120 under the 150 floor.

effectiveness slice, printed p. 74 - the third vision round,
a prose round with a pin-table interior (no printed grid):
pinned as rules/wsgultra.h with the include after wsginfra.h
at line 189 (prefix wuv, free on the first probe). The daylight
bar: infravision is useless in daylight or artificial
illumination stronger than moonlight, the visible light
overriding the heat radiation. The heat-as-light color scale:
1 pitch black (below -50) through 10 excruciatingly bright
(above 130), all ten temperature bands pinned with their
contiguity checked at audit time. The surface-temperature
examples: the 98-degree human brighter than his surroundings
at air 90 or lower, demi-humans the same, the bundled man
matching the air and undetectable save small uncovered
spots; obstruction blocks as with normal vision but a great
heat source is indirectly detectable - the campfire behind
the rock shows as a dark shape on a lighter background. The
extremes: below -50 all pitch black, above 130 blinding, and
sudden close heat (a wall of fire) inflicts heat blindness -
burned out until cure blindness, or temporarily blinded for
5-10 turns (1d6+4). The cold-blooded bar: reptiles, insects
and most nonmammalians undetectable at air temperature, but
magic that abruptly changes the air reveals them briefly.
Ultravision: the ultraviolet night vision - only the deep
gnome has it inborn, to 30 yards as if by daylight normal
vision; others gain it by magic (lens or spell, MU or
illusionist); useless under any light brighter than
moonlight - daylight shows nothing but blackness; best on a
moonless clear night, the five sky modifiers 2/3, 1/2, 1/3,
1/4 and thick cover 1/4 cumulative - the thick forest on a
moonlit overcast night leaving 1/16 of ideal range. THE
